item.title: West New Britain steps up El Nino relief efforts
item.description: The new 10,000-litre capacity water tanker bought by the Talasea DDA Board. (NBC News) A new K376,000 water tanker and supplies of basic food items are being used to help communities in Talasea District affected by the El Niño drought in West New Britain Province.
item.content:encoded:
The new 10,000-litre capacity water tanker bought by the Talasea DDA Board. (NBC News)

A new K376,000 water tanker and supplies of basic food items are being used to help communities in Talasea District affected by the El Niño drought in West New Britain Province.

The water tanker, purchased using El Niño relief funds provided by the National Government, will transport drinking water to communities, particularly in Kimbe Urban and Talasea Local Level Government areas.

Talasea MP Freddie Reu Kumai confirmed the purchase, saying the tanker cost K376,000.

"We have also allocated K1 million of this funding to supply relief supplies, K40,000 for each of the 25 wards in the district," Mr Kumai said.

He said the district was now into its second round of distributing basic food items to affected communities.

Mr Kumai added that other portions of the relief funding would be used to establish water and sanitation facilities.

The water tanker will cover a total of 16 wards; Talasea LLG [10 wards] and Kimbe Urban LLG [6 wards].

Meanwhile, the West New Britain Provincial Government is running a separate El Niño relief programme, focusing mainly on providing water tanks, water and sanitation equipment to affected communities.

Provincial Disaster and Emergency Services Director Clement Bailey said the Provincial Government was also supplying mobile desalination plants to help communities access safe drinking water.

The first desalination equipment has been delivered to the Bali Vitu Local Level Government.

"The desalination equipment will assist locals purify salt water so that they can have access to drinking water," Mr Bailey said.

Mr Bailey clarified that the Provincial Government's relief programme is separate from the support being provided by the respective District Development Authority Boards.

The desalination plant will be stationed at Kumburi village ..Ward 3 Bali Witu LLG ...Bali Island has a total of four wards...so will benefit communities of ward 3 and surrounding wards..

NBC News understands that the Kandrian-Gloucester and Nakanai District Development Authority Boards are also running their own El Niño relief programmes.

item.title: Who is funding PNG’s political party fundraisers?
item.description: Former Prime Minister and Ialibu-Pangia MP Peter O’Neill speaking in Parliament. (Image: National Parliament) Millions of kina raised through political party fundraising events are now under scrutiny.
item.content:encoded:
Former Prime Minister and Ialibu-Pangia MP Peter O’Neill speaking in Parliament. (Image: National Parliament)

Millions of kina raised through political party fundraising events are now under scrutiny.

Former Prime Minister and Ialibu-Pangia MP Peter O’Neill has questioned Administrative Services Minister Richard Masere on who is contributing these huge amounts of money and paying for tables, saying ordinary Papua New Guineans do not have this kind of money.

O’Neill raised this in Parliament on Tuesday.

With just five months remaining before the 2027 National Elections, political parties are busy ensuring they are well organised and prepared for the coming elections.

The parties are carrying out fundraising activities to raise money to support their parties and candidates.

However, these fundraising events have now come under scrutiny following reports of huge amounts of money being paid for tables.

Peter O’Neill questioned why tables are going for K100,000 to K200,000, who is paying for them and whether this complies with the laws governing the registration of political parties.

He alleged that contractors and subcontractors are attending these fundraising events and financing them using money earned from public contracts.

He called on the Government to identify those attending the fundraising events and establish whether they were companies benefiting from government contracts.

Administrative Services Minister Richard Masere pointed out that political party funding and integrity do not fall under his portfolio. He said he would establish which minister or government office is responsible before providing a response to Parliament.

item.title: Wau Waria secures first El Nino relief payments
item.description: (R) Wau Waria DDA CEO, John Orebut presenting the district’s Elnino Assessment Report and first remittance payment advise to ADRA WaSH Snr Project Accountant Dokara Ipu, and the Provincial Disaster Office rep, Jeffrey Sorori (NBC New) The National Banking Corporation (NBC) has finally released the first K786, 987.46 from Wau Waria district's K2.5 million El Nino relief allocation.
item.content:encoded:
(R) Wau Waria DDA CEO, John Orebut presenting the district’s Elnino Assessment Report and first remittance payment advise to ADRA WaSH Snr Project Accountant Dokara Ipu, and the Provincial Disaster Office rep, Jeffrey Sorori (NBC New)

The National Banking Corporation (NBC) has finally released the first K786, 987.46 from Wau Waria district's K2.5 million El Nino relief allocation.

The NBC cleared six urgent payments last week for a diesel water pump, water filtration tanks, medical supplies, three bore water reticulation systems, assessment cost reimbursements to Wau Rural LLG in Morobe.

The payments were processed directly to suppliers following the submission of approved financial documentation, supported by comprehensive drought assessments across all 43 wards, identifying 63,756 affected people from 14,394 households.

From the K786, 987.46, K473,312 is for three bore water reticulation systems. The District Development Authority (DDA) CEO, John Orebut presented the remittance advise as proof of payment to the Adventist Development and Relief Agency PNG (ADRA PNG) recently.

With the advantage of an existing partnership under the district's WASH Programme, ADRA will proceed to drill boreholes at three already surveyed locations to provide water supply for Wau Town.

ADRA's WASH Senior Projects Accountant, Dokara Ipu, commended the district's proactive leadership in preparedness, noting that early feasibility studies and successful electronic payments had positioned Wau Waria for immediate implementation, despite the overwhelming nationwide demand.

A copy of the district's El Nino Assessment Report was also presented to Jeffrey Sorori on behalf of the Provincial Disaster Office, which reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the district.

Mr Orebut acknowledged the collective efforts of ward councillors, ward recorders, LLG presidents and district officers in completing the comprehensive assessments, which also impressed visiting National Weather Service and Provincial Disaster officers.

"We were among the first districts to submit our El Nino Assessment Report, but the new banking system issues delayed access to the funds. We are fortunate and grateful that our MP personally followed up, identified the discrepancies and helped to fast-track the payments," he said.

Relief distribution is expected to commence once outstanding direct supplier payments for water and food rations are cleared this week.

item.title: 36 Chineese nationals are in police custody following clash with Maprik local
item.description: Company’s property burnt down by locals (Supplied) Thirty-six Chinese nationals are in police custody in Wewak following a violent clash with local residents in Kuminimbis, Maprik district, East Sepik Province, which left two locals with serious gunshot injuries and company property destroyed by fire recently.
item.content:encoded:
Company’s property burnt down by locals (Supplied)

Thirty-six Chinese nationals are in police custody in Wewak following a violent clash with local residents in Kuminimbis, Maprik district, East Sepik Province, which left two locals with serious gunshot injuries and company property destroyed by fire recently.

The confrontation involved local residents and Chinese nationals working as alluvial miners in the area. The situation reportedly escalated into violence, resulting in the shooting of two local residents and the destruction of property belonging to Tribal Earth Moving and Construction.

East Sepik Provincial Police Commander Christopher Tamari has assured the National Government and the Chinese Embassy that the 30 nationals are safe and remain in police custody while investigations continue.

"I want to assure the National Government and Chinese Embassy that the Chinese nationals are safe in police custody in Wewak and will not move until the investigation is completed," PPC Tamari said.

Police have placed the workers under protective custody to prevent further retaliation and maintain peace while investigators establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Police have yet to provide further details on the condition of the two injured locals, the extent of the property damage or whether any arrests or charges have been made in connection with the incident.

item.title: Hela Governor announces final phase of Gun Surrender Program
item.description: Hela Gun Surrender Program Coordinator (civilian) checking some of the guns surrendered at Dauli in the Komo Hulia District recently (NBC News) The National Executive Council (NEC)-sanctioned Hela Gun Surrender Programme is entering its final phase, with seven locations remaining before the official closing ceremony on 25 December 2026. The programme aims to encourage voluntary surrender of illega
item.content:encoded:
Hela Gun Surrender Program Coordinator (civilian) checking some of the guns surrendered at Dauli in the Komo Hulia District recently (NBC News)

The National Executive Council (NEC)-sanctioned Hela Gun Surrender Programme is entering its final phase, with seven locations remaining before the official closing ceremony on 25 December 2026. The programme aims to encourage voluntary surrender of illegal firearms, reduce armed violence, end tribal conflicts and restore lasting peace and security across Hela Province.

Led by Governor Philip Undialu as Chairman, with Mathias Manda as Programme Coordinator, the team has planned 24 surrender exercises. So far, 17 have been completed, with seven remaining.

Governor Undialu said to date, the programme has collected over 400 factory-made firearms and more than 2,000 homemade firearms.

“I thank all youth, community leaders, ward councilors, LLG presidents, Local MPs, church elders, women leaders and communities across the 17 locations for responding positively to the call for peace,” he said.

He said the schedule for the other remaining locations are as follows;

Awapia Primary School –Mon, 7 Dec 2026 (8:00 am12:00 noon).

Yuhama Primary– Monday, 7 Dec 2026 (1:00–4:00 pm).

Songura High School – Tuesday, 8 December

Margarima Station – Wednesday, 9 December

Tari Urban / Tari Town – Thursday, 10 December

“The official closing ceremony will take place on Friday, 25 December 2026, at Tari Town, featuring the formal destruction of surrendered firearms and the launch of Phase Two – Youth Training and SME Development Pathway.

Phase Two will focus on youth skills training, entrepreneurship, SME development and sustainable livelihood opportunities,” he said.

Governor Undialu called on all leaders and citizens of Kopiago, Koroba, Margarima and Tari Urban to come forward and voluntarily surrender their illegal firearms during the remaining exercises.

"Walk with me to make Hela Safe Again. Let us build a safer Hela without guns and tribal fights. Let our children pick up books, pencils and computers, whilst parents pick up spades and tools to build homes, grow food and create livelihoods.” He said.

Undialu said Hela will never be the same without guns and tribal fights.

item.title: Pala appointed as acting Labour and Employment Secretary
item.description: Martin Pala is Acting Secretary for the Department of Labour and Employment (Supplied) The National Executive Council has appointed Martin Pala as Acting Secretary for the Department of Labour and Employment.
item.content:encoded:
Martin Pala is Acting Secretary for the Department of Labour and Employment (Supplied)

The National Executive Council has appointed Martin Pala as Acting Secretary for the Department of Labour and Employment.

The appointment was gazetted on November 10, 2026, where Pala will serve in the acting position while the process of appointing a permanent secretary is underway.

Minister for Labour and Employment, Saki Soloma, announced the appointment during a meeting with the department's senior management recently this month.

Minister Soloma said Mr. Pala was not new to the department and possessed valuable institutional knowledge and experience, having witnessed both the successes and challenges faced by the department over the years.

He called on the senior management team to give Mr. Pala their full cooperation and support, emphasising that the department must operate as one team with a shared responsibility to advance the country's labour and employment agenda.

"We are all one team and one family working towards what is best for our country in the area of labour. We must work harder, improve our performance and give our very best in carrying out our responsibilities," the Minister stressed.

Minister Soloma also thanked former acting Secretary George Taunakekei contribution to the department including the establishment of the Minimum Wage Borad and the increase in Minimum wage.

Chief Secretary to Government, Mr Ivan Pomaleu, OBE, said Mr Pala’s appointment would support continuity and accountability within the Department during the transition.

“The public service must remain focused on delivering its responsibilities through any leadership change. I expect Mr Pala to provide clear direction, support staff and ensure the Department continues to meet its obligations to workers, employers and the Government,” he said.

Mr Pala’s work at the Office of Workers Compensation has included introducing the Claims Processing and Payment System to support claims lodgment, tracking and direct payments to claimants.

He has also advanced the review of the Workers Compensation Act 1978 and organisational reform of the OWC. Work is underway to develop a website to further improve access to information and services.

Mr Pala thanked the Government for its confidence and acknowledged Mr Taunakekei’s service.

“My immediate priority is to work with the Minister, management and staff to maintain essential services and keep approved programmes moving,” Mr Pala said.

“We will give staff clear direction, attend to outstanding matters and work with our stakeholders to keep the Department’s work on track while preparing for a smooth handover once a permanent Secretary is appointed.”

item.title: 2027 National Budget ‘deferred to December 1st’
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape announces the deferral of 2027 National Budget (Supplied) Prime Minister James Marape has announced today that the presentation of the 2027 National Budget, originally scheduled for Thursday, 26 November 2026, has been deferred to Tuesday, 1st December 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape announces the deferral of 2027 National Budget (Supplied)

Prime Minister James Marape has announced today that the presentation of the 2027 National Budget, originally scheduled for Thursday, 26 November 2026, has been deferred to Tuesday, 1st December 2026.

This is to allow Treasury officials more time to finalise key measures aimed at easing the cost-of-living pressures facing Papua New Guineans.

“We have asked Treasury to model how best we can provide further relief to our people, particularly through reductions in certain taxes, given the difficult economic circumstances many of our citizens are experiencing.

“Treasury, the Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) and other relevant government agencies are working through this process and require additional time to ensure we get these measures right.” he said.

Prime Minister Marape said the Government also wanted to ensure sufficient funding was allocated for the 2027 National General Election and other government activities to measure the continuing impact of El Niño into next year.

“With our historic return to a balanced Budget after many years, we want to ensure that we get everything right, while providing relief to our people and adequately funding our national priorities.

“Cabinet has supported Treasury’s request for additional time, and we have accordingly moved the presentation of the Budget to next Tuesday.” PM Marape said.

PM Marape confirmed the Budget lock-up is sheulded on Tuesday with the Opposition scheduled to deliver Budget response on Friday, 4 December 2026.

“We want to give the Opposition every opportunity to prepare its response and contribute meaningfully to the Budget debate.

“Our priority is to deliver a responsible, balanced and people-focused Budget that provides relief to our citizens while maintaining fiscal discipline and meeting our national obligations." PM Marape said.

item.title: Papua LNG: Kua warns of collapse, Maladina assures project will continue
item.description: Shadow Petroleum & Energy Minister Kerenga Kua and Simbu Governor Noah Kool at the press conference last Friday. (NBC News) Shadow Minister for Petroleum & Energy, Kerenga Kua warns that the Papua LNG is days away from an imminent total collapse.
item.content:encoded:
Shadow Petroleum & Energy Minister Kerenga Kua and Simbu Governor Noah Kool at the press conference last Friday. (NBC News)

Shadow Minister for Petroleum & Energy, Kerenga Kua warns that the Papua LNG is days away from an imminent total collapse.

He announced this in a press conference on Friday and called on the Prime Minister and Government to take this issue seriously and have it settled before it is too late.

Mr Kua says this could cost the country billions of Kinas, adding the Petroleum Retention License No.15 over Papua LNG has only days remaining before its expiration on 30 November 2026.

He has urged the government to conclude its negotiations with the project area stakeholders for the signing of a Development Agreement, to ensure the continuity of the project and its future development plans.

Mr Kua warns that the imminent collapse of the Papua LNG Project is a matter of great concern as the country stands to lose billions of kinas in investments and revenue

He has also revealed that negotiations on the Petroleum Development License have been boycotted for the past weeks by the Gulf provincial government and landowners.

In a statement released on Sunday, Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina assured the nation that Papua LNG will not collapse when its Retention License expires on 30 November.

According to him, the multi-billion kina project is legally protected under the Oil and Gas Act.
